criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear goal, 4 quantified objectives, and specific users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) linked to needs and to objectives. Benefit to Australia justified with literature references [1]-[6]. Meets accomplished descriptor.

evidence.quote: Mission goal. Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef
Objectives and preliminary requirements. 1. Image the full length of the reef (about 2,300 km)
Users and their needs. The satellite would be operated by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS).

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart weeks 2-10 with completed/planned colours and deadlines. Order justified by mission dependencies, robust contingencies in Table 1 with triggers/responses, and information sources in Table 2. STK choice justified with verification plan.

evidence.quote: The design will be completed in STK (Systems Tool Kit), accessed remotely through the MECH lab 204 licence.
Contingencies. Week 10 is float as well as editing time: no new design work is planned in it.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Good preliminary work: SSO hand calcs (a=6978 km, T=5801 s, 97.8 deg), swath trade, correct period check in STK, and interpretation that weekly coverage not closed. Shows on-track progress.

evidence.quote: I have also made first hand calculations for a candidate orbit, a circular sun-synchronous orbit at 600 km altitude
Interpretation: the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical sections, clear writing, consistent tables/figures with captions, Gantt readable, references cited in text and listed. At professional level, minor OCR artefacts not student errors.

overall: Strong preliminary report: well-scoped reef monitoring mission benefiting Australia, credible 600 km SSO analysis with swath/coverage trade, and exemplary project plan with contingencies.

feedback.summary: Strong preliminary report on your Great Barrier Reef monitoring mission. You scoped a clear goal with quantified objectives, justified users and benefits, completed credible 600 km SSO and swath analysis, and presented an exemplary Gantt and contingency plan. You are well placed for the full mission design.
next_steps: Close your weekly coverage gap by testing neighbouring SSO altitudes or wider swath options in STK and quantify revisit time.
Carry your Table 1 contingency triggers forward and keep Table 2 sources linked to each design decision in the final report.
Extend Table 3 hand calculations into fully verified STK coverage plots over the 2,300 km reef length for the final mission.

criteria.C1: You described a clear reef-colour goal with 4 quantified objectives including imaging the 2,300 km reef, and linked AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO and BoM needs to objectives with references [1]-[6]. To hold Accomplished, keep requirements traceable to users in final design.
criteria.C2: Your Figure 1 Gantt for weeks 2-10 with completed/planned colours and deadlines, dependency ordering, Table 1 triggers/responses including Week 10 float, and Table 2 sources with STK justification is exemplary. To hold Accomplished, follow that sequence through.
criteria.C3: You showed good progress with STK tutorials 1-4, hand calculations for 600 km SSO with a=6978 km, T=5801 s, 97.8 deg, and interpretation that 60 km swath needs 5 passes for 250 km width. To hold Accomplished, convert this into closed coverage results.
criteria.C4: Your report is logical and easy to read with consistent captions for Figure 1 and Table 3, readable Gantt, and in-text references matched to the list. To hold Accomplished, maintain this structure, labelling and referencing discipline in the final report.
